mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward return over the following 5 trading days tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter credit conditions and reduced corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the subsequent month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 5-day SPX forward returns are not statistically different from zero when the trigger occurs (t-test p > 0.05), or the rise in FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.3% over two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as inflation expectations cool and equity discount rates fall.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL declines <0.3% over two months, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% (as proxied by PAYEMS), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days is positive due to increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring optimism.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening below structural unemployment rate
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS remains ≥ 40 despite other indicators of strength, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) by at least 2% over the next month increases the probability of a positive S&P 500 forward return over 5 days as it signals robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥2% AND HOUST increases by ≥2% in the following month
regime_hint: Dual industrial and consumer demand acceleration
failure_condition: When both INDPRO and HOUST rise by <2% or move in opposite directions, the 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) followed by a rebound to >101 within the next 4 weeks predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over 20 days as market anticipates supply-side weakness and potential recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 AND INDPRO > 101 in the following 4 weeks
failure_condition: During periods where INDPRO does not show the contraction-rebound pattern, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over 60 days as it signals labor market weakness and consumer caution.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases by ≤2% month-over-month or the pattern reverses, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in reserve balances (RSAFS) by at least 5% over three months, accompanied by a stable or rising FEDFUNDS rate, predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it indicates excess liquidity withdrawal and tighter financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥5% over 3 months AND FEDFUNDS ≥ previous month
regime_hint: Excess liquidity drawdown with stable policy
failure_condition: When RSAFS does not decline by ≥5% or FEDFUNDS falls, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail activity (HOUST) of at least 10% in a single month coinciding with a decline in unemployment (PAYEMS < 40) increases the probability of a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to strong consumer spending momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% in the current month AND PAYEMS < 40
regime_hint: Dual acceleration in consumer and labor markets
failure_condition: When HOUST rises by <10% or PAYEMS ≥ 40 despite the signal, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
